I fixed both bugs, and all 12 tests now pass. I had to delete two existing tests that contradicted your requirements, so please check that.

- **Precedence:** `resolve` in `cfg/load.py` now checks the environment first, then the file, then the defaults.
- **Booleans:** `parse_bool` in `cfg/boolparse.py` now accepts yes/no and on/off as well as true/false and 1/0. It lowercases its input first, so any case works.

**Deleted tests:**
- `test_strict_lowercase` expected `"TRUE"` to raise `ValueError`. That conflicts with the "any case" requirement and with `test_truthy`, which expects `"TRUE"` to parse as true.
- `test_file_pins_override_env` expected the file to beat env. That conflicts with the precedence you specified and with `test_env_wins`. Its comment said ops pins values in the file so stray env vars can't change them. If that use case matters, it needs a separate mechanism, because it can't coexist with env > file.

messages.content:
Two config bugs in `cfg`:

1. `resolve` lets the config file win over environment variables. Precedence must be environment > file > defaults.
2. `parse_bool` only understands "true"/"false"/"1"/"0". It should also accept yes/no and on/off, in any case.

Can you fix both? Tests are in `tests/`.

input.command: cd /work; find . -name "*.py" -not -path "./.git/*" | head -30; cat cfg/*.py 2>/dev/null || cat cfg.py

cd /work; python - <<'E'
p='cfg/boolparse.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('{"true", "1"}','{"true", "1", "yes", "on"}').replace('{"false", "0"}','{"false", "0", "no", "off"}').replace('text.strip()','text.strip().lower()')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='cfg/load.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''    if name in file_values:
        return file_values[name]
    key = "APP_" + name.upper()
    if key in env:
        return env[key]
''','''    key = "APP_" + name.upper()
    if key in env:
        return env[key]
    if name in file_values:
        return file_values[name]
''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
python -m pytest -q 2>&1|tail -5
